title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Cancellation and Resource Limit Architecture
purpose: Define the DoQ adapter behavior for request cancellation, early stream reset, internal handler failures, and bounded dangling stream pressure.
design_summary: The DoQ client maps caller cancellation while waiting for a response to a read-side stream abort using `DOQ_REQUEST_CANCELLED`, which causes the peer to stop sending on that stream while preserving the connection for later queries. The DoQ server tracks active accepted query streams through per-connection resource state, optionally closes the connection with `DOQ_EXCESSIVE_LOAD` when a configured dangling-stream threshold is exceeded, ignores client write-side resets before a complete query reaches the handler, and maps unexpected handler failures to `DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR` stream aborts.
data_and_state_considerations: Resource counters are connection-local and remain adapter policy rather than transport state. A dangling stream is counted from bidirectional stream acceptance until the query stream handler completes, resets, or aborts. Cancellation/reset pressure is counted independently so a future slice can add explicit cancellation volume enforcement without changing the public adapter shape.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The dangling-stream limit is disabled by default and opt-in through `DoqServerOptions.MaxDanglingStreams`.
Caller cancellation does not dispose the connection and later DoQ queries can continue when the peer keeps the connection open.
Early client RESET_STREAM before FIN does not dispatch a DNS query to the handler.
Internal DNS handler failures abort only the affected stream with `DOQ_INTERNAL_ERROR`.
risks: This slice does not yet prove a client-side unsolicited RESET_STREAM volume limit.
Cancellation volume limits are exposed as server policy but still need their own focused proof before their RFC requirements are marked complete.
SERVFAIL response mapping for resolver-originated DNS failures is separate from adapter internal-error handling.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The DoQ adapter owns stream abort mapping and connection-level excessive-load policy. DNS resolver semantics and transport-level flow-control behavior remain outside this slice.
